hunks.baseline: Sometimes, there are moments when merely witnessing something is enough to send a chill down your spine and make your hair stand on end.
hunks.sol: Sometimes, the mere sight of something sends a chill down your spine and makes your hair stand on end.

hunks.baseline: Like every scene unfolding before my eyes right now.
hunks.sol: Like everything in front of me now.

hunks.baseline: *Fwoosh.*
hunks.sol: *Rustle.*

hunks.baseline: The faint moonlight pouring through the swaying leaves was as mysterious as a scene from a myth, but what it illuminated was not a peaceful blue lake.
hunks.sol: Faint moonlight spilled through the swaying leaves, as mysterious as a scene from a myth. But it wasn’t shining on a peaceful blue lake.

hunks.baseline: *What the……*
hunks.sol: *What is this…?*

hunks.baseline: A swamp steeped in darkness and desolation. Hundreds of enormous shapes, layered in spiderwebs like silkworm cocoons, and pure-white eggs that were smaller but several times more numerous.
hunks.sol: A dark, desolate swamp. Hundreds of large shapes hung there, wrapped in layer upon layer of spiderwebs like silkworm cocoons. Around them were white eggs, smaller but several times more numerous.

hunks.baseline: An ominous question pressed down on my heart, as if it were something I wasn’t supposed to learn the answer to.
hunks.sol: An ominous question weighed on me, one I felt I shouldn’t learn the answer to.

hunks.baseline: But contrary to that thought, the hand I had extended on instinct was already touching the unidentified cocoon hanging closest to me.
hunks.sol: Even so, I’d instinctively reached out. My hand was already touching the nearest cocoon.

hunks.baseline: An unpleasant sensation traveled through my fingertip. At the same time, a System notification pierced my ear.
hunks.sol: An unpleasant sensation ran through my fingertip. At the same moment, a System notification sounded in my ear.

hunks.baseline:
> **System**
>
> - You have been **Poisoned** by **Thousand-Year Spider’s Paralytic Venom**!
>
> - If you are not detoxified quickly, you may enter **Full-Body Paralysis** and **Unconsciousness**!
>
> - The potential effect of the **Myriad-Poison Ring** has been activated!
>
> - All status abnormalities related to **Poison** have been removed!
hunks.sol:
> **System**
>
> - You have been **Poisoned** by **Thousand-Year Spider’s Paralytic Venom**!
> - If you are not detoxified quickly, you may enter **Full-Body Paralysis** and **Unconsciousness**!
> - The potential effect of the **Myriad-Poison Ring** has been activated!
> - All status abnormalities related to **Poison** have been removed!

hunks.baseline: My fingertip, which had felt numb for a moment, soon grew cool and clear.
hunks.sol: My fingertip went numb for a moment, then felt cool and clear again.

hunks.baseline: The Myriad-Poison Ring was a sacred artifact that could even absorb Formless Ultimate Poison. No matter how special a venomous creature the Thousand-Year Spider was, it couldn’t do anything to me.
hunks.sol: The Myriad-Poison Ring was a divine artifact capable of absorbing even Formless Ultimate Poison. However unusual a venomous beast the Thousand-Year Spider might be, its poison couldn’t harm me.

hunks.baseline: *If these really are the Thousand-Year Spider’s webs……*
hunks.sol: *If this is a Thousand-Year Spider’s web…*

hunks.baseline: A guess suddenly flashed through my mind. I put more strength into my hands and pulled the webbing apart from side to side.
hunks.sol: A possibility struck me. I tightened my grip and tore the webbing apart.

hunks.baseline: *Crack. Riiiiip.*
hunks.sol: *Crack. Riiiip.*

hunks.baseline: The hundreds of layers of tangled web tore helplessly under my terrifying grip.
And when the shape concealed inside was revealed, the Beast Miao King, who had been watching from beside me, muttered like he was groaning.
hunks.sol: Hundreds of tangled layers gave way under my grip. When I saw what had been hidden inside, the Beast Miao King let out a groan.

hunks.baseline: “Is that a person?”
hunks.sol: “A person?”

hunks.baseline: A face as white as a sheet of paper. A body that did not move even an inch.
The Beast Miao King checked the unknown man’s slow pulse and let out a sigh of relief.
hunks.sol: The man’s face was as white as paper, and his body lay perfectly still. The Beast Miao King checked the unknown man’s faint pulse and breathed a sigh of relief.

hunks.baseline: “Fortunately, he’s still breathing.”
hunks.sol: “Thank goodness. He’s still alive.”

hunks.baseline: That was something I had expected as well.
According to what the System had told me earlier, the Thousand-Year Spider’s webs did not contain poison powerful enough to kill their victims.
hunks.sol: I’d expected as much. According to the System, the poison in the Thousand-Year Spider’s webs wasn’t meant to kill its victims.

hunks.baseline: And the reason was probably……
hunks.sol: The reason was probably…

hunks.baseline: *To keep them fresh. That way, they can fill their bellies whenever they want.*
hunks.sol: *To keep them fresh. So the spiders can eat whenever they want.*

hunks.baseline: Now I understood why the hair on my body had risen the moment I first set foot here.
hunks.sol: Now I understood why the sight of this place had made my hair stand on end.

hunks.baseline: Before being the Thousand-Year Spider’s habitat, this swamp was a slaughterhouse—and a gigantic food storage facility.
hunks.sol: Before it was the Thousand-Year Spiders’ home, this swamp was a slaughterhouse and an enormous food store.

hunks.baseline: Only then did I notice the deep scent of blood hidden beneath the stench drifting in from every direction. I muttered under my breath.
hunks.sol: Only then did I detect the heavy smell of blood beneath the stench coming from all around us.

hunks.baseline: “Spider bastards. They’ve sure been stuffing their faces for a long time.”
hunks.sol: “Spider bastards. They’ve been eating well for a long time.”

hunks.baseline: If the Nanman Beast Palace’s records claiming that the Five Poisons Sect had created the Poisonblood Grounds were true, then the number of people who had died here over all those years would be impossible to count.
hunks.sol: If the Nanman Beast Palace’s records were right and the Five Poisons Sect had created the Poisonblood Grounds, there was no telling how many people had died here over the years.

hunks.baseline: Ironically, the Thousand-Year Spiders’ habits had made it possible for us to save a great many people today.
hunks.sol: Ironically, the spiders’ habit meant we could save many of their captives today.

hunks.baseline: *It really was strange. More people had disappeared than died.*
hunks.sol: *It did seem strange. More warriors had disappeared than died.*

hunks.baseline: There had been about three hundred elite warriors stationed at Ailao Mountain.

terminology_alerts.message: preferred glossary term appears in BASE but not SOL for this hunk

hunks.baseline: The five Thousand-Year Spiders had definitely killed around a hundred of them on the spot, then, after satisfying their hunger, dragged the rest to the Poisonblood Grounds.
hunks.sol: About three hundred elite warriors had been stationed at Ailao Mountain. The five Thousand-Year Spiders had killed roughly a hundred on the spot, eaten their fill, then dragged the rest into the Poisonblood Grounds. Before long, they would have eaten those warriors one by one.

hunks.baseline: Those people would have been turned into meals one by one before long, but now we had a chance to save them.
hunks.sol: Instead, we’d found them.

hunks.baseline: “Would you look at these goddamn bastards! They deserve to die!”
hunks.sol: “Those goddamn things deserve to die!”

hunks.baseline: I calmed the Beast Miao King, whose eyes had reddened with fury.
hunks.sol: The Beast Miao King’s eyes were red with fury. I tried to calm him down.
“Uh…”

hunks.baseline: Well, I had nothing to say to that. Still, this was a time to focus on dealing with the current situation rather than getting angry.
hunks.sol: Well, I couldn’t argue with that. But for now, we needed to deal with the situation, not dwell on our anger.

hunks.baseline: After calming down a little, the Beast Miao King looked around with a devastated expression.
hunks.sol: After a moment, the Beast Miao King looked around, his expression grim.

hunks.baseline: “To think they dared to do something like this.”
hunks.sol: “To think they were doing this right under our noses.”

hunks.baseline: “You said there hadn’t been any major losses until now, didn’t you?”
hunks.sol: “You said there hadn’t been any major losses before now, didn’t you?”

hunks.baseline: “That is the truth. At least while I have been the Palace Lord, there was never a problem.”
hunks.sol: “It’s true. At least during my time as Palace Lord, we’ve had no trouble like this.”

hunks.baseline: “That’s strange. Five Thousand-Year Spiders suddenly appeared and attacked the warriors at a time like this.”
hunks.sol: “Strange, then. Five Thousand-Year Spiders suddenly show up and attack your warriors at a time like this.”

hunks.baseline: The Beast Miao King fell silent for a moment at my clearly pointed words, then abruptly spoke.

terminology_alerts.message: preferred glossary term appears in BASE but not SOL for this hunk

hunks.baseline: “……Dark Heaven. Do you think this was their doing?”
hunks.sol: He was silent for a moment at my pointed words. Then he said, “Dark Heaven… Do you think this was their doing?”

hunks.baseline: “I don’t know whether they directly laid a hand on this, but they must have exerted some influence. It isn’t strange for a venomous creature like the Thousand-Year Spider to attack people, but considering the timing, we can’t help but suspect them.”
hunks.sol: “I don’t know if they were directly involved, but I’d bet they had a hand in it. There’s nothing strange about Thousand-Year Spiders attacking people. The timing, though? Of course I suspect Dark Heaven.”

hunks.baseline: “But if this truly was Dark Heaven’s doing, they could have waited until after you left. Causing this on the final day of the tribal competition would only harm them.”
hunks.sol: “But if they are behind this, they could have waited until after you left. Doing it on the final day of the Tribal Grand Council only hurts their cause.”

terminology_alerts.message: preferred glossary term appears in BASE but not SOL for this hunk

hunks.baseline: “That…….”
hunks.sol: “Well…”

hunks.baseline: My voice trailed off despite myself. The Beast Miao King’s answer had been sharper than expected, and he had offered evidence I couldn’t easily refute.
hunks.sol: My voice trailed off. His point was sharper than I’d expected, and I couldn’t easily dismiss it.

terminology_alerts.message: preferred glossary term appears in BASE but not SOL for this hunk

hunks.baseline: *He’s not wrong. If I were Southern Heaven Demon Empress—that bitch—I wouldn’t have gone to the trouble of doing this.*
hunks.sol: *He’s right. If I were the Southern Heaven Demon Empress—that bitch—I wouldn’t have bothered.*

terminology_alerts.message: preferred glossary term appears in BASE but not SOL for this hunk

hunks.baseline: Even without any interference, it was practically certain that the Nanman Beast Palace’s entry into the Murim Alliance would fall through. Dark Heaven had no reason to stir up Nanman for nothing.
hunks.sol: The Nanman Beast Palace’s entry into the Murim Alliance had seemed certain to fall through without Dark Heaven lifting a finger. They had no reason to stir up trouble in Nanman.

hunks.baseline: *Then why?*
hunks.sol: *So why?*

hunks.baseline: Everything was shrouded in questions.

Ailao Mountain’s Wraith had appeared out of nowhere and still hadn’t shown itself. Five Thousand-Year Spiders had suddenly begun a massacre. And there was the question of whether they were connected to Dark Heaven.
hunks.sol: None of it made sense. Ailao Mountain’s Wraith had appeared suddenly and then vanished. Five Thousand-Year Spiders had gone on a killing spree out of nowhere. And I had no idea whether any of it was connected to Dark Heaven.

hunks.baseline: I had been frowning in thought for some time when the Beast Miao King’s voice brought me back.
hunks.sol: I was still frowning over it when the Beast Miao King’s voice brought me back.

hunks.baseline: “More importantly, the immediate problem is moving these people. It is a blessing that they are still breathing, but getting back out of the Poisonblood Grounds is another matter.”
hunks.sol: “Right now, the problem is moving these people. It’s a blessing they’re alive, but getting them out of the Poisonblood Grounds is another matter.”

hunks.baseline: I stopped thinking and answered.
“If you ask me, I think it would be better to leave the others as they are.”
hunks.sol: I set those thoughts aside. “If you ask me, we should leave the others as they are.”

hunks.baseline: “Leave them? You mean keep them here?”
hunks.sol: “Leave them? Here?”

hunks.baseline: “……Do I look insane to you? Of course we have to take them back to the Nanman Beast Palace. I told White Tiger to bring the people here, so it would be best to wait. Though I’m not sure he understood me properly.”
hunks.sol: “…Do I look insane? Of course we’re taking them back to the Nanman Beast Palace. I told White Tiger to bring people here, so we should wait for them. Assuming he understood me.”

hunks.baseline: “You must mean Muyaho. He is more intelligent than most people. I am sure he understood you well enough.”
hunks.sol: “You mean Muyaho. He’s cleverer than most people. I’m sure he understood.”

hunks.baseline: “Why are you making that expression?”
hunks.sol: “What’s that look for?”

hunks.baseline: “Oh. It’s nothing. Nothing at all.”
hunks.sol: “Oh. Nothing.”

hunks.baseline: I almost lost it.
hunks.sol: I nearly burst out laughing.

hunks.baseline: Muyaho. The more I heard that name, the less I could get used to it. I barely pulled my crumbling expression back together and continued.
hunks.sol: *Muyaho.* The more I heard that name, the harder it was to get used to. I managed to straighten my face and went on.

hunks.baseline: “And I think we should leave the webs intact instead of tearing them off.”
hunks.sol: “And we should leave the webs intact.”

hunks.baseline: The journey here had been difficult, but the way back would be far worse.

We would have to make our way through the Poison Mist with more than two hundred patients who had only just awakened after spending the past several shichen in a state of full-body paralysis and unconsciousness.
hunks.sol: Getting here had been difficult. Getting back would be far worse. We’d have to take some two hundred patients through the Poison Mist after they woke from several shichen of full-body paralysis and unconsciousness.

hunks.baseline: *I’m not even sure how much the Myriad-Poison Ring can cover.*
hunks.sol: *And I don’t know how many people the Myriad-Poison Ring can protect.*

hunks.baseline: The Myriad-Poison Ring certainly possessed mysterious power, but I couldn’t put two hundred lives through a fifty-fifty gacha roll just by trusting in this one item.
hunks.sol: It had mysterious powers, but I couldn’t stake two hundred lives on a fifty-fifty gacha roll just because I had one divine artifact. They were safer wrapped in the webs.

hunks.baseline: They were safer wrapped in the webs like this.
“At the very least, they don’t seem to be affected by the Poison Mist while they’re inside. If that weren’t the case, they would have all died on the way here.”
hunks.sol: “At least the Poison Mist doesn’t seem to affect them in there. Otherwise, they’d have died on the way here.”

hunks.baseline: “That is true. The Thousand-Year Spider’s poison permeating the webs may be preventing other miscellaneous poisons from getting in.”
hunks.sol: “True. Perhaps the Thousand-Year Spider’s poison in the webs keeps other poisons out.”

hunks.baseline: In a way, it was similar to using poison to suppress poison.
On the way here, the webs had been coffins.
From now on, they would be cryogenic capsules protecting their lives from the Poison Mist.
hunks.sol: In a sense, it was poison countering poison. The webs had been coffins on the journey here. Now they could serve as cryogenic capsules, keeping the warriors safe from the Poison Mist.

hunks.baseline: Even if I took them out one by one and detoxified them, there was a clear limit to what I could do.
At most, our conversation would go something like this.
hunks.sol: Besides, even if I unwrapped and detoxified them one at a time, there was only so much I could do. Our conversations would probably go something like this:

hunks.baseline: *All right, patient. Slowly open your eyes. Can you see the fingers I’m waving in front of you? If you can, tell me how many there are.*
hunks.sol: *All right, patient. Open your eyes slowly. Can you see the finger I’m holding up? How many fingers are there?*

hunks.baseline: “Uuuh. One……one.”
hunks.sol: “Uhh… One. One.”

hunks.baseline: *What finger is it?*
hunks.sol: *Which finger?*

hunks.baseline: *Correct. It means fuck you.*
hunks.sol: *Right. It means fuck you.*

hunks.baseline: “Huh? What are you talking about all of a sudden……?”
hunks.sol: “What? Why would you suddenly…?”

hunks.baseline: *It was a simple test. Anyway, good. You can see and hear clearly now. Both your sight and hearing have recovered.*
hunks.sol: *Just a little test. Anyway, good. You can see and hear properly now. Your sight and hearing have both recovered.*

hunks.baseline: *Ha ha. Think nothing of it. By the way, since you’ve been detoxified, your paralysis should have disappeared. Can you move your fingers?*
hunks.sol: *Ha ha. Don’t mention it. The paralysis should be gone now that you’ve been detoxified. Can you move your fingers?*

hunks.baseline: “Of course. I can move them just fine now.”
hunks.sol: “Of course. I can move them just fine.”

hunks.baseline: *Good. I have something for you to do with those fingers. But before that, may I ask your name?*
hunks.sol: *Good. I have something for you to do with them. First, what’s your name?*

hunks.baseline: “Me? I’m Jang Sam.”
hunks.sol: “Me? Jang Sam.”

hunks.baseline: *Excellent. I’ll give you this dagger. Now write what I say on this wooden tablet.*
hunks.sol: *Excellent. Here’s a dagger. Write what I dictate on this wooden tablet.*

hunks.baseline: “Yes, yes.”
hunks.sol: “Yes, all right.”

hunks.baseline: *All right. Write exactly what I say. Jang Sam.*
hunks.sol: *Write exactly what I say. Jang Sam.*

hunks.baseline: “Lies here. Huh?”
hunks.sol: “Lies here. Wait, what?”

hunks.baseline: *Actually, I didn’t tell you because I was worried you’d panic, but we have to go back the way we came. And we don’t have any poison-warding pearls left. Of course, I’m fine because I have the Myriad-Poison Ring.*
hunks.sol: *I didn’t want to alarm you, but we have to go back the way we came. And we’re out of poison-warding pearls. Oh, I’ll be fine. I have the Myriad-Poison Ring.*

hunks.baseline: There was going to be a two-hundred-to-one bloodbath over the Myriad-Poison Ring.
hunks.sol: That would turn into a two-hundred-against-one battle to the death over the Myriad-Poison Ring.

hunks.baseline: Maybe two hundred to two. The Beast Miao King also possessed a large, beautiful, top-grade poison-warding pearl.
hunks.sol: Or two hundred against two. The Beast Miao King had a big, beautiful top-grade poison-warding pearl of his own.

hunks.baseline: “……Why are you looking at me like that?”
hunks.sol: “…Why are you looking at me like that?” he asked.

hunks.baseline: “No. I mean heaven as in the sky.”
hunks.sol: “No. Heaven as in the sky.”

hunks.baseline: The Beast Miao King’s expression hardened.

hunks.baseline: “Is he really insane……?”
hunks.sol: His expression hardened. “Are you actually insane…?”

hunks.baseline: If my department head had been here, he would have laughed. But it seemed the Palace Lord didn’t get the joke.
hunks.sol: A department head would have laughed, but apparently that joke didn’t work on a Palace Lord.

hunks.baseline: The Beast Miao King looked me over with an expression like he was staring at a Thousand-Year Spider walking on two legs, then began gathering the warriors wrapped in webs into one place.
hunks.sol: The Beast Miao King gave me a look as if I were a Thousand-Year Spider walking on two legs, then began gathering the web-wrapped warriors in one place.

hunks.baseline: Every time his straightened palm moved, the people hanging in midair were neatly stacked together.
hunks.sol: Each sweep of his straightened hand brought more of the people hanging overhead down into a neat pile.

hunks.baseline: There were two hundred of them.
Just as I had guessed, it was almost the same as the number of warriors who had disappeared from Ailao Mountain.
hunks.sol: There were two hundred of them—almost exactly the number of warriors who had gone missing from Ailao Mountain.

hunks.baseline: I had been helping the Beast Miao King move the survivors when I suddenly raised my head at a thought I had temporarily forgotten.

hunks.baseline: One of the questions I had had while searching Ailao Mountain in the beginning: the missing ferocious beasts were nowhere to be seen.
hunks.sol: I was helping him move the survivors when the question I’d forgotten came back to me. The missing ferocious beasts had been one of the mysteries we’d found while searching Ailao Mountain, and there was no sign of them here.

hunks.baseline: The Beast Miao King soon noticed it as well and wore a puzzled expression.
hunks.sol: The Beast Miao King noticed too.

hunks.baseline: “That is strange. There is no sign of the ferocious beasts.”
hunks.sol: “Strange. I don’t see any of the beasts.”

hunks.baseline: “Could they be timid? Maybe they tuck their tails and run away when they meet people they’ve never seen before.”
hunks.sol: “Are they timid, by any chance? Do they tuck their tails and run when they meet strangers?”

hunks.baseline: “I’m asking because I’m curious, but do you perhaps not know what ‘ferocious beast’ means?”
hunks.sol: “I have to ask. Do you know what ‘ferocious beast’ means?”

hunks.baseline: Of course I did. Ferocious. Beast.
hunks.sol: Of course I did. *Ferocious. Beast.*

hunks.baseline: That was precisely why it was strange. So many ferocious beasts wouldn’t have abandoned their master and run off somewhere.
hunks.sol: That was why it was strange. So many of them wouldn’t have abandoned their masters and run away.

hunks.baseline: *It’s not as if the Thousand-Year Spiders are picky eaters, either.*
hunks.sol: *And it’s not as if Thousand-Year Spiders are picky eaters.*

hunks.baseline: This was one thing I knew well. Hope Goshiwon, where I had lived for nearly seven years, had more spiders than hope.[^1]
hunks.sol: I knew spiders. Hope Goshiwon, where I’d lived for nearly seven years, had more spiders than hope.[^1] I’d even grown fond enough of them to share my ramen.

hunks.baseline: Eventually, I had even grown fond enough of them to share my ramen.
*Then where the hell did they go?*
hunks.sol: *Then where the hell did the beasts go?*

hunks.baseline: We would have to search the Poisonblood Grounds more thoroughly to find out, but the Thousand-Year Spiders didn’t seem meticulous enough to sort their food into separate categories.
hunks.sol: We’d have to search more of the Poisonblood Grounds to find out, but I doubted Thousand-Year Spiders were meticulous enough to sort their food by type.

hunks.baseline: And it was at that exact moment, while the Beast Miao King and I were looking around with puzzled expressions—
hunks.sol: Just as the Beast Miao King and I were looking around in confusion—

hunks.baseline: Along with a small noise, I sensed a faint presence more than ten zhang away.
hunks.sol: A small sound came from more than ten zhang away. With it, I sensed a faint presence.

hunks.sol: [^1]: A goshiwon is an inexpensive housing arrangement of very small rooms, often with shared facilities.
